result:
If I could change one thing, I'd make humans significantly better at long-term thinking and cooperation at scale.

Right now, we're pretty good at solving problems when they're immediate, personal, or tribal. We're much worse at coordinating around slow-moving, complex threats (climate, AI risk, demographic collapse, antibiotic resistance, etc.) because our psychology is still largely wired for small groups and short time horizons. A modest but consistent upgrade in our collective ability to think clearly about the future and act on it—even when it requires short-term sacrifices—would probably unlock more progress than almost any other single change.

Everything else (poverty, disease, conflict, environmental damage) becomes much more tractable if we get better at not constantly shooting ourselves in the foot for near-term advantage. The hard part isn't usually the technical solution; it's getting enough people to prioritize the real problem over status, signaling, and zero-sum games.

So: better calibration between our intelligence and our wisdom. That one lever moves a lot.
